citations.title: Policy and procedure manual
citations.requirement: Manual for organization and operation must be developed, implemented and reviewed at least annually. Each review is documented. The manual is available in the facility to DOH representatives at all times. It must include: (1) organizational chart showing lines of authority; (2) description of services the facility can provide; (3) security policies; (4) abuse/exploitation reporting to the DOH Complaints Program at 1-800-792-9770, plus the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995 if the resident is 60 or older; (5) confidentiality and release of records; (6) personnel records; (7) employee physicals, immunizations and TB testing; (8) prompt notification of a resident's death. Under (b), a policy must say how manuals are made available to residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, applicants and referring agencies.

citations.title: Resident care policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Written resident care policies must be established, implemented and reviewed at intervals the policies specify, with each review documented. They must include control of smoking under N.J.S.A. 26:3D-55 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 8:6 (subsection (a)8). Other required items (a)1-7 and 9-11 were not shown in the text retrieved.

citations.title: Posting and distribution of statement of resident rights
citations.requirement: Each provider must post and distribute a statement of resident rights to residents of ALRs, CPCHs and ALPs. Retrieved items: #27 confidential treatment of information; #37 written notice at least 30 days before a facility-requested transfer or discharge, except in an emergency, including the Ombudsman's name, address and phone, and also given to the guardian or, with consent, the family; #40 right to complain without threat or reprisal, with names, addresses and phones of complaint agencies (DOH and the State LTC Ombudsman) given to the resident, guardian and family member and posted conspicuously. The NJ Ombudsman rights summary also lists freedom from chemical and physical restraints and from physical and mental abuse and neglect.

citations.title: Reportable events
citations.requirement: Notify the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately by phone at (609) 633-9034, or (609) 392-2020 after business hours, followed by written confirmation within 72 hours, of: (1) termination of the administrator, with the replacement's name and qualifications; (2) any elopements; (3) suspected resident abuse or exploitation reported to the State LTC Ombudsman. The written notice goes to the Division.

citations.title: Admission and retention of residents
citations.requirement: (a) The administrator or designee interviews the resident (and family, guardian or agency if the resident agrees) at or before admission, covering policies, business hours, fees, services, resident rights and admission/discharge criteria, with the interview documented in the record. (b) Emergency-contact information is voluntary, and admission cannot be denied for declining it. (c) If a resident's behavior shows danger to self or others and the facility cannot provide proper care, the attending or on-call physician decides on placement and mental health screening is initiated under N.J.S.A. 30:4-27.1 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 10:31. (d) An applicant denied admission after a written application must, on written request, receive a signed written reason within 15 days of receipt of the request. (e) Infirmary transfer requires consent and is generally limited to one week.

citations.title: Involuntary discharge
citations.requirement: Written notice from the administrator to the resident and family, guardian or designee. Discharge only on grounds stated in the policies, of which the resident was informed in advance. Notice at least 30 days ahead, stating the reason and the right to appeal, with a copy in the record. The 30-day notice does not apply to discharge for reasons in 5.1(d). Emergency transfer for life safety is allowed without 30 days' notice, and DOH must be notified.

citations.title: Types of services provided to residents
citations.requirement: (a) Provide or coordinate personal care and services based on assessment by qualified persons, consistent with the Nurse Practice Act and N.J.A.C. 13:37. (b) Be capable of personal care, nursing, pharmacy, dining, activities, recreation and social work services. (c) Supervise self-administration and have trained, supervised staff administer medications. (d) Be capable of nursing services including nursing-home-level residents. A resident may, but need not, be moved if the record documents one of 8 characteristics (24/7 nursing supervision; bedridden over 14 days; totally dependent in 4 or more ADLs; severe cognitive decline; stage 3/4 or multiple stage 2 pressure sores; needs more than assistance with transfer; danger to self or others; unstable condition). A single stage 2 sore must be retained with a plan of care. (e) The admission agreement must say whether the facility will retain such residents, to what extent and at what added cost. (f) Residents needing specialized long-term care must be transferred. (h)-(l) A new ALR or CPCH licensed on or after 9/1/2001 must reach 10% Medicaid-eligible occupancy within 3 years and maintain it. Added beds must be 10% Medicaid-occupied. With fewer than 10 beds, at least one bed is reserved. The Commissioner may waive or reduce the requirement, and must waive it if funding is limited.

citations.title: Minimum personal care assistant staffing
citations.requirement: On the premises at all times: at least one awake personal care assistant and at least one additional employee. With more than one free-standing building with residents, at least one PCA in each building, and both PCAs must then be awake. These levels are a minimum only. Staff must be sufficient in number and training based on an assessment of resident acuity.

citations.title: Qualifications of personal care assistants
citations.requirement: A PCA is a facility employee who completed a DOH-approved nurse aide course (N.J.A.C. 8:39-43) and passed the NJ Nurse Aide Certification Exam, or a DOH-approved PCA course and competency evaluation leading to PCA certification. PCA certification requires the criminal history background check under N.J.A.C. 8:43I. Certification is valid 2 years and renewal requires an updated check. Each PCA and direct caregiver gets orientation before or on employment and ongoing in-service on assisted living concepts. Under (m), a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation triggers DOH review and possible entry on the PCA abuse registry with a disciplinary hearing.

citations.title: Certified medication aides
citations.requirement: A certified medication aide must complete a DOH-approved medication administration course and pass a DOH-approved exam. Renewal is every 2 years with at least 10 hours of continuing education per period (5 hours on fundamentals of medication administration and 5 on drug use relevant to the elderly). A finding of abuse, neglect, misappropriation, negligence or incompetence can lead to the medication aide abuse registry. DOH gives notice with at least 30 days to request a hearing.

citations.title: Storage and control of medications
citations.requirement: The administrator provides a safe storage area for medications that are not self-administered (a locked medication cart is acceptable). Medications are stored per manufacturer or pharmacy directions and kept in original, labeled containers. Generic substitutes are labeled per N.J.A.C. 8:71. Needles and syringes are stored, used and disposed of per N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5.10 et seq., N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7, N.J.A.C. 7:26-3A and 29 CFR 1910.1030, with a record of purchase, storage and disposal. Controlled dangerous substances follow N.J.S.A. 24:21-1 et seq. Theft of scheduled or controlled substances is reported to the NJ Dept. of Law and Public Safety, Enforcement Bureau of Professional Boards at (973) 648-4742 and/or other authorities with jurisdiction.

citations.title: Development of infection control policies and procedures
citations.requirement: (c) Document annual influenza vaccination for each resident per the ACIP recommendations of 8/27/2021, unless contraindicated or refused. Vaccination of accepting residents is completed by November 30 each year. Residents admitted after that date, up to February 1, are vaccinated before or on admission as medically appropriate unless they refuse. (d) Document pneumococcal vaccination for residents 65 and older per ACIP (1/28/2011), or provide or arrange it before or on admission unless refused.

citations.title: General infection control policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Written infection prevention and control policies must be established and implemented. Needles and syringes that residents use in home self-care are disposed of per N.J.S.A. 2C:36-6.1 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7. Other required topics (18.3(a)1-7) were not shown in the text retrieved.

citations.title: Staff training program for Alzheimer's disease and dementia
citations.requirement: A facility that advertises or holds itself out as having an Alzheimer's disease or dementia program must train all licensed and unlicensed staff who give direct care to residents with Alzheimer's or dementia, per N.J.S.A. 26:2M-7.2. Copies of the mandatory training program are available from the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations on written request.

citations.title: Submission and availability of documents
citations.requirement: On request, the facility submits in writing any documents the chapter requires to the Director of the CN&L Program. On DOH request it also submits utilization, demographic, cost, charge and staffing data. The facility reports resident days for the prior calendar year to the CN&L Program by April 15 each year.

citations.title: Transfer of ownership
citations.requirement: Before ownership is transferred, the prospective new owner applies to the CN&L Program. After review DOH sends an approval letter with licensure forms and a fee request. Within 5 working days after the transaction closes, the applicant submits the required follow-up documents. The rule fee is $1,500 (see 8:36-2.2).

citations.title: Application for licensure
citations.requirement: A license application is made to the Commissioner after a Certificate of Need is received. The applicant forwards the ALR/CPCH admission agreement to the CN&L Program for review, to confirm it does not violate the chapter, CON conditions or State/Federal law. The application includes the commitment that at least 20% of residents will have nursing-home-level needs within 36 months of licensure. Fees are nonrefundable: $1,500 + $15 per bed initial and annual, $1,500 biennial inspection, $1,500 transfer of ownership, $375 relocation. Applicants may request a preliminary conference with the CN&L Program.

citations.title: Newly constructed or expanded facilities
citations.requirement: Plans go to the DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit for approval before construction. The license application includes the Unit's written final release. Before occupying a new or renovated building, the facility submits a local certificate of occupancy to the Unit and further items to the CN&L Program.

citations.title: Surveys
citations.requirement: DOH's Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations surveys once the written application is approved and the building is ready. A license issues after a preliminary conference and submission of local zoning, fire, health and building approvals plus a certificate of occupancy or certificate of continued occupancy. No resident may be admitted before written DOH approval or a license, and violators face penalties under N.J.S.A. 26:2H-14 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-1.

citations.title: Surrender of license
citations.requirement: Notify each resident, the resident's physician and guarantors of payment at least 30 days before voluntary surrender of a license, or as directed under an order of revocation, non-renewal or suspension. Return the license to the CN&L Program within 7 working days.

citations.title: Waiver
citations.requirement: A facility seeking a waiver of the chapter applies in writing to the Director of the CN&L Program. 8:36-5.1(l)2 uses this process for waiver of the 10% Medicaid occupancy requirement.

citations.title: Advertisement of assisted living
citations.requirement: Only facilities licensed as ALRs or CPCHs may describe and offer themselves to the public as providing assisted living services.

citations.title: Qualifications of the administrator
citations.requirement: The administrator must be at least 21, hold a high school diploma or equivalent, and hold a current NJ nursing home administrator license or NJ assisted living administrator certification. A qualified owner may serve. Candidates sit the competency exam within two years of the training course and complete a criminal background check. Renewal requires at least 30 hours of CE on assisted living topics earned within the certificate period, and a background check. The certificate runs 3 years.

citations.title: Actions against an assisted living administrator
citations.requirement: An administrator's certificate may be revoked, suspended or restricted for improper practice. Improper practice includes a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property of a resident of an ALR, CPCH or ALP, or of a patient, resident or client of any other DOH-licensed facility or agency.

citations.title: Notices
citations.requirement: Conspicuously post a notice that specified information is available in the facility during business hours to residents and the public. The posted information includes the DOH toll-free hotline, county agency phone numbers and the State LTC Ombudsman number (#6). The other items (#1-5, #7) were not shown in the text retrieved.

citations.title: Health care assessment and health service plan
citations.requirement: (a) Within 30 days before admission, a physician, advanced practice nurse or physician assistant states in writing that the resident is appropriate for this level of care. At admission, the administrator and resident arrange the physician and dentist to call. (c) If the initial assessment shows health care needs, an RN completes a health care assessment within 14 days of admission, using the DOH instrument or an equivalent. (d) The assessment covers ADLs, cognition, communication/hearing, vision, physical functioning, continence, psychosocial well-being, mood and behavior, and activity patterns. (e) A written health service plan is developed from the assessment.

citations.title: Initial assessments and resident service plans
citations.requirement: Upon admission, each resident receives an initial assessment by a registered professional nurse to determine the resident's needs (text as quoted in a DOH survey citation). Text of 7.1(b)-(f), including the general service plan timeline, was not retrieved from the official code.

citations.title: Nursing services (registered nurse availability)
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: at least one registered professional nurse must be available at all times, and each resident receives an RN assessment and care plan. What 'available' means for coverage and response time must be confirmed with DOH.

citations.title: Supplemental Security Income recipients (CPCH)
citations.requirement: Each CPCH must annually have at least 5% of residents be SSI-eligible, at least half of them former psychiatric patients. The percentage is computed on resident days per calendar year and reported to the CN&L Program by April 15 for the prior year.

citations.title: Assisted living program service provider requirements
citations.requirement: ALP services must be delivered only inside a licensed ALR, CPCH or publicly subsidized housing (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Notices (ALP)
citations.requirement: The ALP provider and each program site post a notice that specified information is available at the site and at the provider's main office. It includes the DOH hotline, county senior-services agency numbers and the State LTC Ombudsman number.

citations.title: Notification requirements (ALP)
citations.requirement: With the resident's consent, notify the family, guardian or designated person promptly of specified events. These include any serious accident, criminal act or incident causing serious harm or injury, or the resident's arrest or detention, in which case the CN&L Program is also notified in writing. The ALR counterpart is 5.15 (text not retrieved).

citations.title: Reportable events (ALP)
citations.requirement: ALPs notify DOH immediately by phone at (609) 633-9034 or (609) 392-2020 after hours, with written confirmation within 72 hours. Events include reportable infections and diseases under N.J.A.C. 8:57 among residents (#4) and suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation reported to the State LTC Ombudsman (#7).

citations.title: Requirements for dining services
citations.requirement: Nutrients and calories for each resident follow the Dietary Reference Intake tables of the Food and Nutrition Board (National Academies), adjusted for age, sex, weight, physical activity and therapeutic needs. Subchapter 10 also sets qualifications for dietitians and designation of a food services coordinator (per the readoption summary).

citations.title: Fire extinguisher specifications
citations.requirement: Fire extinguishers must comply with NFPA 10, Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers, 2002 edition.

citations.title: Resident environment (pets)
citations.requirement: If pets are allowed, the facility provides safeguards to prevent interference in residents' lives. Guidelines for pet-facilitated therapy are available from DOH.

citations.title: Criminal Background Investigations: Nurse Aides, Personal Care Assistants, and Assisted Living Administrators
citations.requirement: Applicants for certification or recertification as a nurse aide, PCA or assisted living administrator submit to a criminal history record background check. There is a process for a determination of rehabilitation after a disqualifying conviction. Readopted effective 1/17/2024, expiring 1/17/2031.

citations.title: Background checks for nurse aide and personal care assistant certification
citations.requirement: A follow-up federal criminal history check is required at least every two years as a condition of recertification of each certified nurse aide and PCA. The Commissioner may provide an alternative means.

citations.title: State minimum hourly wage
citations.requirement: NJ minimum wage is $15.92/hour effective 1/1/2026. NJDOL publishes the CPI-adjusted 2027 rate around September 30, 2026, which was not checked.

citations.title: Medicaid per diem for assisted living (statutory minimums and Medicaid-volume tiers)
citations.requirement: Sets minimum Medicaid per diems for ALR/CPCH/ALP and tier add-ons by yearly average Medicaid census, measured from paid claims against total licensed beds: $10 at 15% to under 30%, $15 at 30% to under 50%, $30 at 50% to under 70%, $35 at 70% or more. The SFY2026 base is $91.10 (ALR), $81.10 (CPCH) and $79.10 (ALP) per DHS notice of 7/16/2025. SFY2027 rates and CMS approval were not checked.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: An ALR provides apartment-style housing and congregate dining for four or more unrelated adults. Units have at minimum one unfurnished room, a private bathroom, a kitchenette and a lockable entrance door. A CPCH provides room and board, with units of no more than two residents and a lockable door. 'Licensed nurse' means an RN or PN licensed under N.J.A.C. 13:37. Contact details: CN&L Program, PO Box 358, Trenton 08625-0358, (609) 292-6552; Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations, PO Box 367, Trenton 08625-0358, (800) 792-9770; DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit, (609) 633-8151.

citations.title: State Long-Term Care Ombudsman notification (as cited in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a)4)
citations.requirement: When a resident is 60 or older, alleged or suspected abuse or exploitation must also be reported to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995. Only the rule's cross-reference was retrieved, not the statute text.

citations.title: Emergency medical services
citations.requirement: Subchapter 14 covers emergency medical services, emergency plans and procedures, and drills and tests (per the DOH readoption summary). Secondary summary only (not the official code): written plan for emergency transport, a CPR/Heimlich-trained employee available at all times, and an AED on site with a trained employee available. Confirm against the code text.

citations.title: Emergency plans and procedures
citations.requirement: Section 14.2 (Emergency plans and procedures) is confirmed in the DOH readoption summary and the chapter table of contents. Its text was not retrieved, so the specific content must be pulled before finalizing. Staff in-service must cover emergency plans and procedures (secondary source).

citations.title: Drills and tests
citations.requirement: Section 14.3 (Drills and tests) is confirmed in the chapter table of contents. Drill frequency and content were not retrieved and must be pulled from the code text.

citations.title: Record retention
citations.requirement: Subchapter 15 covers health record, record availability, confidentiality, record retention, register, individual records and record of death (confirmed in the chapter table of contents and the DOH readoption summary). A DOH survey deficiency text quotes a 10-year retention period after discharge for all records. The section number-to-text match and the period must be confirmed in the code.

citations.title: Record of death
citations.requirement: 8:36-5.7(a)8 requires a policy on staff responsibility for prompt notification of a resident's death as required by N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5e and N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7(a). The text of 15.7 itself was not retrieved.

citations.title: Quality Improvement (quality improvement programs, use of restraints, personal care services)
citations.requirement: Subchapter 21 sets standards for quality improvement programs, the use of restraints and personal care services (DOH readoption summary). Specific section numbers and text (21.1-21.3) must be pulled before citing at section level.

citations.title: Resident activities
citations.requirement: Subchapter 12 (sole section 12.1) establishes standards for provision of resident activities. 5.1(b) also requires capability to provide activities, recreational and social work services. Detailed content was not retrieved.

citations.title: Social Work Services
citations.requirement: Subchapter 13 (13.1-13.2) establishes qualifications of social workers and requirements for social work services (DOH readoption summary). Detailed content was not retrieved.

citations.title: Housekeeping, Sanitation, Safety and Maintenance
citations.requirement: Subchapter 17 (17.1-17.8) sets standards for housekeeping, laundry, pest control, resident environment, waste removal, sanitation, and heating and air conditioning (DOH readoption summary). The DOH Affidavit of Compliance lists a written housekeeping work plan with trained staff. Section-level content was not retrieved.

citations.title: Standards for Respite Care Services
citations.requirement: Subchapter 20 (20.1-20.3) covers purpose and scope, policies and procedures, and staffing for respite care (DOH readoption summary). It applies only if respite is offered. Detailed content was not retrieved.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved. Secondary summaries say all personnel get orientation at hire and at least annual in-service on assisted living concepts, emergency plans, infection control, resident rights, abuse and neglect, pain management, and dementia care. Confirm against the code.

citations.title: Staffing requirements
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved. Pull the text before stating requirements (staffing in sufficient number for resident needs per secondary source).

citations.title: Financial arrangements and full disclosure
citations.requirement: The DOH readoption summary says subchapter 6 requires full disclosure of the costs of services. The section number and title for 6.2 come from an older compilation, and the text was not retrieved. Confirm against the code.

citations.title: Personal needs allowance
citations.requirement: The DOH readoption summary says subchapter 6 requires a personal needs allowance policy. The section number comes from an older compilation, and the text was not retrieved. Confirm against the code.

citations.title: Resident transportation
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Written agreements
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved. Likely covers contracts with outside providers; confirm.

citations.title: Maintenance of records
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Notification requirements
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved. A 2017 compilation (secondary) says the family, guardian or designee is notified when known and with consent, immediately after events such as acute illness needing medical care. Confirm. The ALP counterpart 23.8 is verified.

citations.title: Interpretation services
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Referral and transfer agreements
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Managed risk agreements
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed in the table of contents; text not retrieved. An HHS compendium (secondary) says a facility must seek to negotiate a managed risk agreement when a resident's choice poses a high probability of risk.

citations.title: Social Isolation Prevention (13A.1-13A.11)
citations.requirement: Subchapter 13A is listed in the chapter table of contents but is not described in the DOH 2021 readoption notice (added later). Text not retrieved. Pull it before drafting, since it adds required policy content.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Administrator Responsibilities and Organizational Chart
state_specifics: Organizational chart shows lines of authority, responsibility and accountability for administration and resident care (5.7(a)1).
Administrator: age 21+, HS diploma or equivalent, and a current NJ nursing home administrator license or NJ assisted living administrator certification. A qualified owner may serve.
Termination of the administrator is reportable to DOH immediately by phone, with the replacement's name and qualifications and written confirmation within 72 hours (5.10).
An administrator certificate may be revoked, suspended or restricted after a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation (8:36-3.5).
DOH contacts: CN&L Program (609) 292-6552; Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations (800) 792-9770.

policies.title: Description of Services the Facility Is Capable of Providing
state_specifics: Manual must describe services the ALR/CPCH/ALP can provide: personal care, nursing, pharmacy, dining, activities, recreation and social work (5.1(b)).
State the license type (ALR: apartment-style housing and congregate dining; CPCH: room and board, units of no more than 2 residents).
Describe capability for nursing-home-level residents and the retention limits in 5.1(d).
Describe medication services: supervised self-administration and administration by trained, supervised staff.
Keep consistent with the admission agreement and any advertising (2.10).

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Advertising, Waivers, Surrender of License and Change of Ownership
state_specifics: No admission before written DOH approval or a license; penalties under N.J.S.A. 26:2H-14 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-1.
Only licensed ALRs and CPCHs may advertise or offer assisted living services (2.10).
Fees (nonrefundable): $1,500 + $15 per bed annually; $1,500 biennial inspection; $1,500 transfer of ownership; $375 relocation.
Waivers: apply in writing to the Director of the CN&L Program (2.7). Surrender: 30 days' notice to residents, physicians and payment guarantors; return license within 7 working days (2.6).

Ownership transfer: the new owner applies to CN&L before transfer; follow-up documents are due within 5 working days after closing (5.3). Post the 5.11 notice, including the DOH hotline and Ombudsman number.

policies.title: Licensure Application Narratives: Design, Neighborhood Integration, Waivers and Nursing-Home-Level Access
state_specifics: Evaluate any waivers sought under 2.7 (2.2(e)4).
Describe how the architecture promotes privacy, choice, independence, dignity and a home-like environment (2.2(e)5).
Describe how the physical plant serves residents with reduced mobility, incontinence and dementia (2.2(e)6).
If plans are required under 2.3, describe how the location promotes physical integration or social connection with existing services and amenities (2.2(f)).
Plans go to the DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit before construction; the application includes the Unit's written final release.

policies.title: Policy and Procedure Manual: Annual Review, Availability and Document Control
state_specifics: Manual is developed, implemented and reviewed at least annually. Each review is documented (name, date, changes).
Manual is available in the facility to DOH representatives at all times.
Written procedure for making manuals available to residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, prospective applicants and referring agencies (5.7(b)).
Resident care policies (6.1) are reviewed at the intervals the policies specify, and each review is documented.
ALP: manual available at every ALP site, the provider main office and to DOH (23.4).

policies.title: Quality Improvement and Performance Review
state_specifics: Subchapter 21 sets standards for quality improvement programs. Pull the section-level text before citing 21.1-21.3.
Track incidents, reportable events, falls, infections, grievances and elopements, and review them at least quarterly.
Track progress on the 20% nursing-home-level and 10% Medicaid-eligible commitments.
Document corrective actions after each DOH survey.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity (NJ FamilyCare / MLTSS)
state_specifics: Bill NJ FamilyCare/MLTSS plans only for services actually delivered and documented in the service plan.
Medicaid does not pay room and board; resident cost share is billed per the plan and county determination.
Per diem tier add-ons are measured from yearly paid claims against total licensed beds. Do not budget them until confirmed in writing by DMAHS.
Designate a compliance contact and keep a hotline or reporting channel with a non-retaliation statement.

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities (Posting and Distribution)
state_specifics: Post and distribute the DOH statement of resident rights (4.1(a)) to all residents of the ALR, CPCH or ALP.
Rights include confidential treatment of information and freedom from chemical and physical restraints and from abuse and neglect.
Give a copy at admission and document receipt.
Conspicuously post the 5.11 notice (DOH hotline, county agency numbers, Ombudsman).
For MLTSS residents, apply HCBS settings protections (privacy, choice, lockable unit door).

policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: Residents may complain to the administrator, staff, government agencies and anyone else without threat, interference, discharge or reprisal.
Give each resident, guardian and family member the names, addresses and phone numbers of DOH and the State LTC Ombudsman, and post them conspicuously.
DOH Complaints Program: 1-800-792-9770. State LTC Ombudsman: 1-877-582-6995.
Allow Ombudsman access to residents and records as the law provides.
Log each grievance, investigation, response and outcome.

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits, Refunds and Notice of Charge Changes
state_specifics: Send the ALR/CPCH admission agreement to the CN&L Program for review at application. It must not violate the chapter, CON conditions or State/Federal law.
Agreement lists charges for room, board, all levels of service and care, and additional services (6.2; section text to be confirmed).
Agreement states how and when residents are notified of charge changes and their right to request written justification of an increase.
Agreement states the right to appeal involuntary discharge (5.14(b)) and the 5.1(d) discharge criteria, how discharge is implemented, which staff take part and the extent of resident participation.
Agreement states whether the facility retains residents with 5.1(d) characteristics, to what extent and at what added cost (5.1(e)). Counsel reviews deposit and refund terms.

policies.title: Resident Funds, Personal Needs Allowance and Personal Property
state_specifics: Written personal needs allowance policy (6.3; confirm section text).
Resident funds are held only with written consent, kept separate from facility funds, with receipts and a quarterly statement.
MLTSS residents: DMAHS 2026 figures are room $996.40/month and personal needs $147.65/month (effective 1/1/2026). Verify before billing.
Inventory of personal property at admission and discharge.

policies.title: Advance Directives and Resident Choice
state_specifics: Ask about advance directives and health care representatives at admission and record the response.
Honor valid directives; staff do not witness or draft them.
Place a copy in the record and give it to EMS or the hospital at transfer.
Have counsel confirm the NJ advance directive statute text before finalizing.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality, Release of Records and HIPAA
state_specifics: Confidential treatment of resident information is a resident right (4.1(a)27).
Procedures for examination of records by the resident and other authorized persons.
Release of records outside the facility only as the resident consents or as required by law or a third-party payor.
Notice of privacy practices and a designated privacy officer.
Records are kept secure, and access is limited by role.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination, Language Access and Interpretation Services
state_specifics: Interpretation services are provided as 8:36-5.16 requires (confirm section text).
Admission decisions are based on the admission criteria and the facility's capability, not on protected status.
Provide reasonable accommodations and auxiliary aids, and post nondiscrimination and language-assistance notices.
Document each interpreter use.

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Admission Interview and Denial of Admission
state_specifics: Within 30 days before admission, a physician, APN or PA states in writing that the resident is appropriate for this level of care (7.2(a)).
The administrator or designee interviews the resident, and family or guardian if the resident agrees, at or before admission. Document the interview in the record (5.13(a)).
Emergency-contact information is voluntary, and admission cannot be denied for declining it.

If an applicant's behavior is dangerous to self or others and proper care is not possible, the attending or on-call physician decides on placement. Mental health screening follows N.J.S.A. 30:4-27.1 and N.J.A.C. 10:31.
A denied applicant who requests it in writing receives a signed written reason within 15 days.

policies.title: Nursing-Home-Level Access, Medicaid-Eligible Occupancy and CPCH SSI Commitments
state_specifics: Within 36 months of licensure, at least 20% of residents have nursing-home-level needs, computed on resident days per calendar year.
ALR/CPCH licensed on or after 9/1/2001: at least 10% Medicaid-eligible occupancy within 3 years, then maintained. Added beds must be 10% Medicaid-occupied. Fewer than 10 beds: reserve at least one.
The Commissioner may waive or reduce the Medicaid requirement (apply under 2.7).
CPCH only: at least 5% of residents SSI-eligible each year, at least half of them former psychiatric patients. Report to CN&L by April 15.
Track the percentages monthly and keep admissions and acuity records for survey.

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
state_specifics: An RN does the initial assessment upon admission (7.1(a)).
If needs are identified, an RN completes the health care assessment within 14 days of admission using the DOH instrument or an equivalent.
Assessment covers ADLs, cognition, communication/hearing, vision, physical functioning, continence, psychosocial well-being, mood and behavior, and activity patterns.
Reassess on any change of condition. Confirm the periodic reassessment interval against 7.1(b)-(f) text, which was not retrieved.
MLTSS: coordinate with the plan care manager on level-of-care and assessment documents.

policies.title: Health Service Plan / Care Plan and Managed Risk Agreements
state_specifics: A written health service plan is developed from the RN assessment (7.2(e)).
Each resident has an RN assessment and care plan (8.2).
Resident and representative take part in planning, and the resident's choices are documented.
When a resident's choice poses a high probability of risk, seek to negotiate a managed risk agreement (5.18; confirm text).
Service plan lists the services, the staff responsible and the review dates.

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: A resident may, but need not, be moved if the record documents one of the 8 characteristics in 5.1(d): 24/7 nursing supervision; bedridden over 14 days; totally dependent in 4+ ADLs; severe cognitive decline; stage 3/4 or multiple stage 2 pressure sores; needs more than assistance with transfer; danger to self or others; unstable condition.
A single stage 2 pressure sore must be retained with a plan of care.
Residents needing specialized long-term care must be transferred (5.1(f)).
The admission agreement states retention, extent and added cost (5.1(e)).
Infirmary transfer requires consent and is generally limited to one week (5.13(e)).

policies.title: Involuntary Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Written notice from the administrator to the resident and to the family, guardian or designee at least 30 days in advance, stating the reason and the right to appeal. Keep a copy in the record.
Discharge only on grounds stated in the policies, of which the resident was told in advance.
Notice includes the Ombudsman's name, address and phone. It goes to the guardian, or to the family with the resident's consent.
The 30-day notice does not apply to 5.1(d) reasons. Emergency transfer for life safety is allowed without 30 days' notice, and DOH is notified.
If the license is surrendered, revoked or not renewed, give 30 days' notice to residents, physicians and guarantors (2.6).

policies.title: NJ FamilyCare MLTSS Participation, Per Diem and Room-and-Board Billing
state_specifics: SFY2026 base per diem: $91.10 ALR, $81.10 CPCH, $79.10 ALP. SFY2027 rates and CMS approval were not checked.
Tier add-ons by yearly average Medicaid census: $10 at 15% to under 30%; $15 at 30% to under 50%; $30 at 50% to under 70%; $35 at 70% or more.
Medicaid does not pay room and board. Verify the 2026 DMAHS standards of $996.40 room and $147.65 personal needs.
MLTSS eligibility: nursing-home level of care, resource and income limits. Refer families to the county agency or a benefits specialist.
Confirm in writing with DMAHS and each plan whether EVV applies to ALR-based services.

policies.category: Assisted Living Program (ALP) (only if licensed as an ALP)
policies.title: Assisted Living Program Contracts, Manual, Notices and Reporting
state_specifics: ALP services are delivered only inside a licensed ALR, CPCH or publicly subsidized housing.

The ALR/CPCH and the licensed program keep written contracts detailing all policies, procedures and services (23.2). A written contract with the subsidized housing unit goes in the application (2.2(l)1).
Provider-resident agreement for each site is submitted with the application and addresses 23.3(d) (2.2(l)2).
Manual follows 5.7 and is available at every ALP site, the main office and to DOH (23.4).
Post the 23.6 notice at each site and the main office. Notify family or guardian of serious events (23.8). Report events to DOH under 23.17(b).

policies.title: Resident Care Policies and Procedures Index and Review
state_specifics: Written resident care policies are established, implemented and reviewed at the intervals the policies set. Each review is documented.
6.1(a) lists items 1-11; only item 8 (smoking control) was retrieved. Pull items 1-7 and 9-11 from the official code and map each to a policy before use.
Cross-reference each 6.1 item to the policy that covers it.
Staff sign the policy acknowledgement at orientation and after each revision.

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage, Disposal and Theft Reporting
state_specifics: The administrator provides safe storage for medications that are not self-administered (a locked medication cart is acceptable).
Store per manufacturer or pharmacy directions in original, labeled containers. Label generic substitutes per N.J.A.C. 8:71.
Needles and syringes: store, use and dispose per N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5.10 et seq., N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7, N.J.A.C. 7:26-3A and 29 CFR 1910.1030, with a purchase, storage and disposal record.
Controlled dangerous substances follow N.J.S.A. 24:21-1 et seq.
Report theft of Scheduled or Controlled Substances to the NJ Dept. of Law and Public Safety, Enforcement Bureau of Professional Boards, (973) 648-4742, and/or other authorities with jurisdiction.

policies.title: Medication Administration, Self-Administration and Staff Authorization
state_specifics: Supervise self-administration, and have trained, supervised staff administer medications (5.1(c)).
Certified medication aide: DOH-approved course and exam. Renewal every 2 years with at least 10 CE hours (5 on fundamentals, 5 on drug use in the elderly).
A finding of abuse, neglect, misappropriation, negligence or incompetence can lead to the medication aide abuse registry. DOH gives at least 30 days to request a hearing.
Keep the CMA certificate and CE records in the personnel file.

policies.title: Nursing Services, RN Availability and Delegation
state_specifics: At least one RN available at all times, and each resident has an RN assessment and care plan (8.2). Confirm with DOH what 'available' means for coverage and response time.
Services follow the Nurse Practice Act and N.J.A.C. 13:37. 'Licensed nurse' means an RN or PN licensed under N.J.A.C. 13:37.
Facility must be capable of nursing services, including for nursing-home-level residents (5.1(d)).
Define which tasks may be delegated and to whom, with RN supervision.

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Notify the physician promptly of an acute change; unstable condition is a 5.1(d) retention characteristic.
Notify family, guardian or designee with the resident's consent (5.15; confirm text).
Call 911 first for emergencies. Send the face sheet, medication list, directives and contacts with the resident.
Keep referral and transfer agreements current (5.17; confirm text).
Document the event and file an incident report if 5.10 applies.

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
state_specifics: If the facility advertises or holds itself out as having an Alzheimer's or dementia program, train all licensed and unlicensed direct-care staff in specialized care (N.J.S.A. 26:2M-7.2).
Copies of the mandatory training program are available in writing from the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations.
Document curriculum, dates and attendance.
Severe cognitive decline is a 5.1(d) characteristic. Danger to self or others requires the 5.13(c) process.

policies.title: Falls Prevention and Post-Fall Response
state_specifics: Fall risk is assessed using the physical functioning and cognition domains of the RN assessment (7.2(d)).
Interventions go into the health service plan.
Post-fall: assess, notify physician and family as needed, and document.
Serious injury triggers incident and family notification (5.15; confirm text).

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Management
state_specifics: Stage 3 or 4, or multiple stage 2, pressure sores are a 5.1(d) characteristic permitting transfer.
A single stage 2 sore must be retained with a plan of care.
RN documents the skin assessment at admission and when the condition changes.
Include turning, positioning and nutrition measures in the service plan.

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
state_specifics: Written agreements with outside providers (5.9; confirm text).
Retention of residents with 5.1(d) characteristics must be documented in the record.
Coordinate the hospice or home health care plan with the facility service plan. Define who gives which care.
The admission agreement states whether hospice residents are retained and at what cost.

policies.title: Death of a Resident and Prompt Notification
state_specifics: Staff responsibilities for prompt notification of a resident's death as required by N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5e and N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7(a).
Notify physician, family or designee and others as directed.
Complete the record of death (15.7). Confirm section text.
Release of remains and belongings follows the resident's documented wishes and legal requirements.

policies.title: Social Work Services and Respite Care (if offered)
state_specifics: Facility must be capable of social work services (5.1(b)). Subchapter 13 sets social worker qualifications and requirements.
Respite care applies only if offered. Subchapter 20 covers purpose and scope, policies and procedures, and staffing.
Respite residents get the same assessment, service plan and rights as other residents.
Pull section-level text before citing subchapters 13 and 20 in the final manual.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report all alleged and suspected resident abuse or exploitation to the DOH Complaints Program at 1-800-792-9770.
If the resident is 60 or older, also notify the State LTC Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995.
Suspected abuse reported to the Ombudsman is also a reportable event: call DOH (609) 633-9034 immediately, or (609) 392-2020 after hours, with written confirmation within 72 hours.
Findings of abuse, neglect or misappropriation can lead to the PCA or medication aide abuse registry and to action against an administrator certificate.
Staff training and non-retaliation protection; apply the 'immediately' standard to every report.

policies.title: Incident, Accident and Reportable Events Reporting
state_specifics: Notify the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately at (609) 633-9034, or (609) 392-2020 after hours, then confirm in writing within 72 hours.
Reportable under 5.10: termination of the administrator (with replacement's name and qualifications), any elopements, and suspected abuse or exploitation reported to the Ombudsman.
ALP also reports reportable infections and diseases under N.J.A.C. 8:57 (23.17(b)).

With consent, notify family or guardian of serious accidents, criminal acts or incidents causing serious harm, or the resident's arrest. Notify CN&L in writing as well (23.8; ALR counterpart 5.15, confirm).
Post the numbers and train every shift lead.

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Any elopement is reportable to DOH immediately by phone, with written confirmation within 72 hours.
Missing-resident search procedure, call to 911 and notification of family or guardian.
Identify residents at risk through the assessment. Include them in the service plan.
Review the incident and revise the plan afterward.

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Freedom from chemical and physical restraints is a resident right (4.1(a)).
Subchapter 21 sets standards for the use of restraints. Pull the section text before final.
Seclusion and punitive restrictions are prohibited.
Document any permitted use, the physician order, monitoring and alternatives tried.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness, Disaster Plan and Emergency Medical Services
state_specifics: Written plans for medical emergencies, power failures, fire and natural disasters (14.2). The text was paraphrased from a third-party source, so verify it against the official code.
Plans are filed with DOH, and DOH is notified of changes.

Procedures specify who is notified, how notification is verified, equipment and alarm locations, evacuation routes and procedures, re-entry and recovery, fire drill frequency, staff tasks, and medications and records to take.
Secondary source only: a CPR/Heimlich-trained employee and an AED with a trained employee at all times. Confirm against 14.1.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Fire extinguishers comply with NFPA 10 (2002 edition) (16.15).
Drill frequency and content (14.3): pull the code text before finalizing.
Local fire approval and a certificate of occupancy or continued occupancy are required for licensure.
Keep alarm, sprinkler and extinguisher inspection records.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control, Immunizations and Resident Needle/Syringe Disposal
state_specifics: Written infection prevention and control policies (18.3(a)); items 1-7 were not retrieved and must be pulled from the code.
Needles and syringes used by residents in home self-care are disposed of per N.J.S.A. 2C:36-6.1 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7 (18.3(a)8).
Influenza vaccination documented annually, completed by November 30. Residents admitted after that, up to February 1, are vaccinated before or on admission unless they refuse.
Pneumococcal vaccination for residents 65 and older per ACIP, documented or provided unless refused.
Exposure control plan under 29 CFR 1910.1030.

policies.title: Smoking Control, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: Control of smoking per N.J.S.A. 26:3D-55 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 8:6 (6.1(a)8).
If pets are allowed, provide safeguards to prevent interference in residents' lives (17.3(b)7). DOH has pet-facilitated therapy guidelines.
Visitor policy respects resident rights and privacy.
Post designated smoking areas, if any.

policies.title: Security Policies and Procedures
state_specifics: Written procedures for maintaining security, including entry control, visitor sign-in and key control.
Each unit has a lockable entrance door (ALR/CPCH).
Night-time rounds and staff awareness of exits.
Coordinate with the elopement and emergency policies.

policies.title: Food Service, Dining and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Nutrients and calories for each resident follow the Food and Nutrition Board Dietary Reference Intake tables, adjusted for age, sex, weight, activity and therapeutic needs (10.5(c)6).
Subchapter 10 sets dietitian qualifications and a designated food services coordinator.
Congregate dining is required for an ALR (dining services).
Therapeutic diets are ordered by a physician and recorded in the service plan.

policies.title: Activities, Social Programming and Social Isolation Prevention
state_specifics: Facility must be capable of activities, recreation and social work services (5.1(b)). Subchapter 12 (12.1) governs resident activities.
Subchapter 13A (Social Isolation Prevention) is listed in the table of contents. Its text was not retrieved, so pull it before drafting.
Offer activities matched to resident interests and abilities, including residents with dementia.
Record participation.

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry, Pest Control and Maintenance
state_specifics: Subchapter 17 (17.1-17.8) covers housekeeping, laundry, pest control, resident environment, waste removal, sanitation, and heating and air conditioning.
Written housekeeping work plan with trained staff.
Regulated medical waste and sharps handling.
Maintain a work-order log.

policies.title: Resident Transportation
state_specifics: Transportation policy per 5.8 (confirm text).
Written plan for emergency transport.
Staff drivers: license, vehicle insurance and training. Wheelchair securement.
Say in the admission agreement which transportation is included and which costs extra.

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Supervision and Wage Compliance
state_specifics: At least one awake PCA and one additional employee on the premises at all times (9.3).
With more than one free-standing building with residents, at least one PCA in each building, and both PCAs awake.
These levels are minimums only. Staffing must be sufficient in number and training based on an assessment of resident acuity.
At least one RN available at all times (8.2).
NJ minimum wage is $15.92/hour from 1/1/2026. Check the 2027 rate when NJDOL publishes it. Overtime and companionship-exemption rules follow FLSA home care rules.

policies.title: Background Checks, Registries and Staff Certification Verification
state_specifics: PCA certification requires a criminal history background check under N.J.A.C. 8:43I. Certification is valid 2 years, and renewal requires an updated check (N.J.S.A. 26:2H-83 et seq.).
Administrator certification and recertification also require a background check.
Check the PCA and medication aide abuse registries before hire.
Keep proof of certification in the personnel file. Do not schedule anyone before screening is complete.

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: PCA: DOH-approved nurse aide course plus NJ Nurse Aide Certification Exam, or DOH-approved PCA course and competency evaluation.
Each PCA and direct caregiver receives orientation before or on employment and ongoing in-service on assisted living concepts (9.1).
Other in-service topics under 5.5 (emergency plans, infection control, rights, abuse and neglect, dementia): confirm against the code.
Dementia training is required if a dementia program is advertised.
Document orientation and in-service in the personnel file.

policies.title: Employee Health, Physical Examinations, Immunizations and Tuberculosis Screening
state_specifics: Specify content and frequency of physical examinations, immunizations and tuberculin testing on employment and afterward.
Applies to employees and to individuals giving direct resident care through contractual arrangements or written agreement.
Offer hepatitis B vaccination to employees with occupational exposure.
Records of physical examinations go in the personnel file.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each employee file includes name, previous employment, educational background, credentials, license number with effective and expiration dates, certification, and verification of credentials.
Also records of physical examinations, job description, records of orientation and inservice education, and job performance evaluation.
Include background check and registry results, PCA/CMA certificate dates and CE.
Keep files secure and available to DOH.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Prohibit abuse, neglect and misappropriation. A finding can lead to registry entry or action on an administrator certificate.
No borrowing from, gifts from, or financial dealings with residents.
Confidentiality of resident information.
Mandatory reporting of suspected abuse by all staff.

policies.title: Administrator Qualifications, Certification Renewal and Continuity
state_specifics: Age 21+, HS diploma or equivalent, and a current NJ nursing home administrator license or NJ assisted living administrator certification.
Candidates sit the competency exam within 2 years of the training course and complete a criminal background check.
The certificate runs 3 years. Renewal requires at least 30 CE hours earned within the period, plus a background check.
Report administrator termination to DOH immediately, with the replacement's qualifications (5.10).
DOH Certified Assisted Living Administrators office: 609-633-9706.

policies.title: Resident Records, Confidentiality and Retention
state_specifics: Subchapter 15 covers health record, availability, confidentiality, retention, register, individual records and record of death.
A DOH deficiency text quotes a 10-year retention period after discharge. Confirm the period and section number in the code before adopting.
Each record holds the admission interview, physician statement, RN assessment, health service plan, notices and incident reports.
Records are available to DOH on request.

policies.title: Required Reports and Submissions to the State
state_specifics: Report resident days for the prior calendar year to the CN&L Program by April 15 each year.
On request, submit required documents in writing to the Director of CN&L, and utilization, demographic, cost, charge and staffing data.
Reportable events: immediate phone report, written confirmation within 72 hours.
Emergency plans filed with DOH, and DOH notified of changes.
CPCH: report SSI-eligible percentage by April 15.

documents.title: N.J.A.C. 8:36 – Standards for Licensure of Assisted Living Residences, Comprehensive Personal Care Homes, and Assisted Living Programs (sections that list required written policies and procedures: 2.2, 4.1, 5.7, 5.10, 6.1, 11.7, 14.2, 18.3, 19.3, 23.4)
documents.form_number: None. I found no single DOH policy checklist form, so the regulation sections are used instead.
documents.issuer: NJ Department of Health (Certificate of Need and Licensing Program; Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations)
documents.version: Current codified text as shown on Cornell LII. §§ 2.2 and 5.7 show 'Amended by 54 N.J.R. 54(a), effective 1/3/2022'. Chapter readopted with technical changes and now expires 2028. I did not verify whether the 2026 proposal (PRN 2026-003) was adopted.
documents.how_used: Primary source for the policy and procedure manual list in § 5.7(a)(1)-(8) and (b), which applies to ALRs, CPCHs and ALPs. Also used for the admission agreement in § 2.2(c), the application narratives in § 2.2(e)-(f) and (l), and §§ 6.1, 14.2, 18.3 and 23.4, which require other written policies.

documents.title: N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2 Application for licensure (current text)
documents.form_number: None. The license application forms themselves are prescribed by the Department and are excluded here.
documents.how_used: Lists the admission agreement content and the application narratives that are policy or program content. Fee, track record, physical plant and bed-count items are excluded.

documents.title: Notice of Readoption with Technical Changes, N.J.A.C. 8:36 (NJ DOH)
documents.issuer: NJ Department of Health, Certificate of Need and Licensing Division
documents.how_used: Official DOH PDF giving the chapter's subchapter structure. It also gives the revised text of § 5.7(a)(4), § 6.1(a)(8), § 4.1(a)(37) and (40), § 11.7(l), § 18.3(a)(8), § 19.3(a) and § 5.10(a). It contains only the technical changes, not the full chapter.

documents.title: AAS-24 Affidavit of Compliance, Assisted Living Residences, Comprehensive Personal Care Homes and Assisted Living Programs
documents.issuer: NJ Department of Health, Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations
documents.version: Undated. I saw only a search excerpt and could not fetch the full form.
documents.how_used: Supporting source only. It lists the N.J.A.C. 8:36 mandatory standards the administrator attests to, including '6.1 (a) 1-11 Written resident care policies and procedures'. No items are drawn from it.

required_items.text: A policy and procedure manual(s) for the organization and operation of the facility or program shall be developed, implemented, and reviewed at least annually. Each review of the manual(s) shall be documented, and the manual(s) shall be available in the facility or program to representatives of the Department at all times. The manual(s) shall include at least the following:
An organizational chart delineating the lines of authority, responsibility, and accountability for the administration and resident care services of the facility or program;
A description of the services which the assisted living residence, comprehensive personal care home or assisted living program is capable of providing;
Policies and procedures for maintaining security;

Policies and procedures for reporting all alleged and/or suspected cases of resident abuse or exploitation to the Complaints Program of the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations at 1-800-792-9770. If the resident is 60 years of age or older, the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman shall also be notified, in compliance with N.J.S.A. 52:27G-7.1 et seq., at 1-877-582-6995;

Policies and procedures for maintaining confidentiality of resident records, including policies and procedures for examination of resident records by the resident and other authorized persons and for release of resident records to any individual outside the facility or program, as consented to by the resident or as required by law or third-party payor;

Policies and procedures for the maintenance of personnel records for each employee, including at least his or her name, previous employment, educational background, credentials, license number with effective date and date of expiration (if applicable), certification (if applicable), verification of credentials, records of physical examinations, job description, records of orientation and inservice education, and evaluation of job performance;

Policies and procedures, including content and frequency, for physical examinations and immunizations and tuberculin testing upon employment and subsequently for employees and individuals providing direct resident care services in the facility through contractual arrangements or written agreement; and

Policies and procedures delineating the responsibilities of the facility's staff in making prompt notification regarding the death of a resident as required by N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5e and N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7(a).

The facility shall have a policy and procedure that addresses how policy and procedure manuals will be made available to residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, prospective applicants, and referring agencies.

A policy and procedure manual(s) for the organization and operation of the assisted living program shall be developed, implemented and reviewed in accordance with the provisions of N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7. The manual(s) shall be available in all assisted living program sites, the assisted living program provider main office, and to representatives of the Department. (Assisted living programs only.)

Written resident care policies and procedures shall be established, implemented, and reviewed at intervals specified in the policies and procedures. Each review of the policies and procedures shall be documented. Policies and procedures shall include, but not be limited to, the following: 1.-11. [I could not retrieve the full text of items 1-7 and 9-11; see notes. The readoption notice confirms only item 8, below.]
The control of smoking in the facility, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 26:3D-55 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 8:6;

A copy of the assisted living residence or comprehensive personal care home admission agreement or other document stating the scope of a facility's services shall be forwarded to the Director of the Certificate of Need and Licensing Program for review when application for licensure is made. [Does not apply to a CCRC's continuing care agreement.] The admission agreement shall include, but not be limited to, the following:
Proposed charges for room, board and all levels of service and care and for all additional services and care not included in the standard package of rates in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.2;

Specification of how and when the resident will be notified of any change in charges, and a statement that each resident has the right to request written justification of any increase in charges in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.2;
A statement that each resident has the right to appeal an involuntary discharge as specified at N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.14(b); and

Specification of the criteria identified at N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d) which will be used to discharge residents and an explanation of how the discharge process will be implemented, including which facility staff will participate and the extent of resident participation.
An evaluation of any requested waivers to licensing requirements that are sought in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.7;
A description of how the architectural design will promote the essential values of assisted living, including privacy, choice, independence, dignity and a home-like environment;
A description of how the physical plant will facilitate the care of residents with common long-term care problems, such as reduced mobility, incontinence and dementia; and

A statement of the proposed licensed operator's commitment to assuring access to assisted living for individuals with nursing home level of care needs, as defined in N.J.A.C. 8:36-1.3. This statement shall indicate that within 36 months after licensure, at least 20 percent of the facility's residents shall be individuals with nursing home-level of care needs. This percentage shall be computed based on the number of resident days per calendar year and may include direct admissions as well as maintained residents with nursing home-level of care needs.

If an applicant is required to submit plans under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.3, the applicant shall submit a description of how the location of the proposed facility will promote the physical integration or social connection of the residents into a neighborhood, center or other area with existing services or amenities.

For assisted living programs, the application shall include a copy of the written agreement or contract between the program provider and residents that will be used at each program site, including clearly addressing N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.3(d). [Also 2.2(l)1: a copy of the written contract between the program provider and the publicly subsidized housing unit in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.2(c).]

Each assisted living provider shall post and distribute a statement of resident rights for all residents of assisted living residences, comprehensive personal care homes, and assisted living programs. [Items 1-42 are the rights listed in the rule. Two items are quoted below.]

The right to receive written notice at least 30 days in advance when the facility requests the resident's transfer or discharge, except in an emergency. This written notice shall include the name, address, and telephone number of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, and shall also be provided to the resident's legally appointed guardian, if applicable, or, with the resident's consent, to the resident's family, 30 days in advance;

The right to voice complaints without being threatened or punished. Each resident is entitled to complain and present his or her grievances to the administrator and staff, to government agencies, and to anyone else without fear of interference, discharge, or reprisal. The facility shall provide each resident and his or her legally appointed guardian, if applicable, and the resident's family member with the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the government agencies to which a resident can complain and ask questions, including the Department and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman. These names, addresses, and telephone numbers shall also be posted in a conspicuous place in the facility;

The facility shall notify the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately by telephone at (609) 633-9034 or (609) 392-2020 if after business hours, followed within 72 hours by written confirmation, of the following: [items 1-3; item 3 is any suspected cases of resident abuse or exploitation which have been reported to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman]. (Assisted living programs: see 23.17(b).)

Any theft of Scheduled or Controlled Substances shall be reported to the New Jersey Department of Law and Public Safety, Enforcement Bureau of Professional Boards at (973) 648-4742, and/or to any other municipal, county, State, or Federal authority having jurisdiction over theft of such substances.

The facility shall develop written emergency plans, policies, and procedures which shall include plans and procedures to be followed in case of medical emergencies, power failures, fire, and natural disasters. The emergency plans shall be filed with the Department and the Department shall be notified when the plans are changed. Procedures for emergencies shall specify persons to be notified, process of notification and verification of notification, locations of emergency equipment and alarm signals, evacuation routes, procedures for evacuating residents, procedures for reentry and recovery, frequency of fire drills, tasks and responsibilities assigned to all personnel, and shall specify medications and records to be taken from the facility upon evacuation and to be returned following the emergency. [Paraphrased from a third-party transcription (alfboss.com). Subsection letters were not captured. Verify against the official text.]

Written policies and procedures shall be established and implemented regarding infection prevention and control, including, but not limited to, policies and procedures for the following: 1.-7. [not retrieved; see notes]
Needles and syringes used by residents as part of home self-care shall be disposed of in accordance with N.J.S.A. 2C:36-6.1 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7, and amendments thereto.

A facility that advertises or holds itself out as having an Alzheimer's disease or dementia program shall provide training in specialized care of residents who are diagnosed by a physician as having Alzheimer's disease or dementia to all licensed and unlicensed staff who provide direct care to residents with Alzheimer's or dementia, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 26:2M-7.2. (Applies only to facilities that advertise such a program.)

The assisted living residence and/or the comprehensive personal care home shall establish and maintain written contracts detailing all policies, procedures, and services to be provided by the licensed facility and the licensed program. (Assisted living programs only.)

official.notes: I found no single NJ DOH policy-review checklist or application packet for this license. The required content comes from the N.J.A.C. 8:36 sections listed above. Reviewers should treat § 5.7(a)(1)-(8) and (b) as the core manual list. It applies to ALRs, CPCHs and ALPs, and the manual may be one document or several. The manual must be developed, implemented and reviewed at least annually. Each review must be documented, and the manual must be available at the facility or program for Department representatives at all times. An ALP must also keep it at every program site and at the provider's main office (§ 23.4). The Department states the manual should be available to residents, guardians and referring agencies under a written policy (§ 5.7(b)). With the license application, the ALR or CPCH admission agreement goes to the Director of the Certificate of Need and Licensing Program for review (§ 2.2(c)). An ALP submits its resident agreement and its contract with the publicly subsidized housing unit (§ 2.2(l)). Written emergency plans must be filed with the Department, and the Department must be told when they change (§ 14.2, per a secondary source). A preliminary conference with the CN&L Program is optional (§ 2.2(n)). Survey by the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations follows application approval and precedes licensure and admission of residents (§ 2.4). The Department publishes an Affidavit of Compliance (AAS-24) that cites the chapter's mandatory standards, including § 6.1(a)(1)-(11). Gaps and cautions: (1) I could not retrieve the verbatim lists in § 6.1(a)(1)-(7) and (9)-(11) or § 18.3(a)(1)-(7). Pull them from the Cornell LII pages for N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1 and 8:36-18.3 before using them. (2) The § 14.2 text is from a non-official transcription and should be checked against the official text. (3) I did not review §§ 7.1, 10.x, 11.x, 20.x or 21.x for further written-policy requirements, such as respite care policies, restraint policy, quality improvement and dining. A complete checklist should add them. (4) Excluded as non-policy content: fees, track-record evaluation, physical plant and bed-count description (§ 2.2(e)1-3), plan review, certificate of occupancy, and local approvals. (5) The 2026 proposed rule changes to §§ 1.3 and 2.4 (CPCH deemed status) have not been verified as adopted.
